attacks.claim: The no-overwrite guarantee and the public 'stay put' promise are contradicted by the sync rule. When only the cloud copy is newer, the game silently replaces the local slot with no prompt, and only the both-changed case asks the player.
attacks.evidence: "Nothing is overwritten without that choice." and "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older." and patch notes: "Your saves on this PC stay where they are."

attacks.claim: The silent-overwrite decision relies on device-reported last-modified timestamps, which are not server-authoritative. A device with a wrong clock can make a newer local save look older and get replaced without a prompt.
attacks.evidence: "sync.meta" sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name); "the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older"

attacks.claim: 1.3 does not update the sidecar. A save played on 1.3 can carry a stale last-modified value, so 1.4 may treat the local slot as unchanged and silently replace it with the cloud copy.
attacks.evidence: "1.3 ignores the sidecar, so a player moved back to 1.3 keeps a working save." and "Nothing is overwritten without that choice."

attacks.claim: The first link of a second store has no last-sync baseline, so the 'both changed since last sync' rule is undefined there. The artifact does not say what happens when two non-empty saves exist at link time.
attacks.evidence: "If both changed since last sync, the game asks" / ABSENT: first-link merge behavior for existing local and cloud saves

attacks.claim: Upload is several files (slots plus sidecar) with no stated atomicity. A partial failure can leave a slot and its sidecar out of step, causing a wrong copy to be picked or a false conflict.
attacks.evidence: "Sync uploads the existing save slots plus a small `sync.meta` sidecar" / ABSENT: transactional or all-or-nothing upload semantics

attacks.claim: Automatic deletion after 24 months of inactivity can destroy a player's only surviving copy, for example after a lost PC. Unlink also permanently deletes server copies, which may hold the newest progress, with no notice, confirmation or grace period. This conflicts with the agreed 'never lose a save' rule.
attacks.evidence: "Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted" and "removes the link and all server copies within 24 h (local saves untouched)" / ABSENT: pre-deletion notice, confirmation or undo

attacks.claim: The 1.3 rollback is only described as restoring the 1.3 default branch on both stores. No Epic 1.3 build is evidenced, and changing the default branch does not downgrade players already on 1.4. The only downgrade test ran on a Steam beta branch.
attacks.evidence: "1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores" vs QA row: "Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)" / ABSENT: Epic 1.3 build and the path that moves 1.4 players back

attacks.claim: The 1.3 downgrade was tested only for loading. Nothing shows that a 1.3 session that rewrites a save keeps the 1.4 modifier keys. A silent strip would persist after returning to 1.4.
attacks.evidence: "Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored" / ABSENT: round-trip test showing 1.3-written saves retain the 1.4 options keys

attacks.claim: The Epic production sign-in and token path was not tested on a shipping build. QA used the Epic dev sandbox build against production, and the Steam build is on a private branch with no evidence it matches the public binary. Epic is 29% of players and the release is all-at-once.
attacks.evidence: "Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox" and "Steam build 18204411 on a private branch" / ABSENT: production-build test with production EOS config and binary identity check

attacks.claim: Launch sync is a thundering herd of about 182k players at 10:00 PT on day one, but the load test covers only 30k concurrent launches over 10 minutes with no stated peak assumption. No client retry, backoff or timeout behavior is specified, and the 60 uploads/hour cap can be hit on repeated launches.
attacks.evidence: "Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min" and "60 uploads per hour per player" / ABSENT: client retry and backoff policy

attacks.claim: The kill switch, the primary rollback control, has no QA row. Its automatic flip at the budget stop has no described mechanism or test, and the hard budget stop's effect on stored data is unstated. Clients re-read the switch only every 10 minutes.
attacks.evidence: "Kill switch `cross_save_enabled=false` (server config, read on launch and every 10 min)" and "at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically." / ABSENT: kill-switch QA row and budget-stop test

attacks.claim: The under-13 restriction is applied only to Epic cabined accounts. Steam accounts have no age gate, and EU minors aged 13 to 15 are not addressed, so minors' Steam IDs can be linked to Epic IDs.
attacks.evidence: "Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered" / ABSENT: age gate for Steam accounts and for EU minors

attacks.claim: The 'no name' claim may be inaccurate. The device name in sync.meta is stored server-side and can be personal, such as a real name in a PC hostname, and the artifact does not say it is sanitized or length-limited.
attacks.evidence: "device name" in sync.meta vs "No email, name, payment or friends data." / ABSENT: device-name validation or disclosure

attacks.claim: Consent is not explicit. The policy is only linked from the screen, and no acceptance step is described for the steam_id↔epic_account_id pairing.
attacks.evidence: "linked from the Cross-Save screen before linking" / ABSENT: explicit acceptance step

attacks.claim: Retention for the identity link record is unspecified. The 24-month rule covers only cloud data, so the link may persist indefinitely.
attacks.evidence: "Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted" / ABSENT: link-record retention

attacks.claim: Beta participants linked accounts and uploaded saves, but the artifact does not show PP-v6 applied to beta collection or describe beta data deletion.
attacks.evidence: "public opt-in beta branch on Steam (2,300 players) and Epic sandbox testers (150)" / ABSENT: beta-period notice and deletion

attacks.claim: Logs and monitoring may contain steam_id and epic_account_id. No redaction or retention rule is stated, and access/export and backup/replica deletion are not covered.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: log redaction, retention, data export and backup deletion; "removes the link and all server copies within 24 h"

attacks.claim: Tokens expire after 1 h, but revocation on unlink is not stated. A token outstanding after unlink could still read or write slots during the 24 h deletion window.
attacks.evidence: "tokens are scoped to one player and expire after 1 h" / ABSENT: token revocation on unlink

attacks.claim: A checksum is not an authenticated integrity check. The client loads cloud blobs after checksum and schema checks only, with no stated parser hardening.
attacks.evidence: "The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading" / ABSENT: MAC or signature and parser hardening

attacks.claim: A well-formed but bad upload becomes the newest version, and five uploads can push out good history. The server keeps no quarantine or head rollback, and 'Every replaced version is kept' overstates the 5-version retention.
attacks.evidence: "the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot" and "Every replaced version is kept" / ABSENT: server-side quarantine or head rollback

attacks.claim: No alerts cover blob rejections, upstream Steam/EOS token failures, kill-switch state, or the owner of the $250 billing alert.
attacks.evidence: "Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores" / ABSENT: alerts for validation failures, kill-switch state and spend-alert owner

attacks.claim: QA ran against the production Cross-Save backend and config, but no cleanup of test accounts, links or server copies is described.
attacks.evidence: "pointed at the production Cross-Save backend with the production config." / ABSENT: test-data cleanup
